- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review

## Answers

**h01 — S3 presign refresher**
- **Component:** `s3presign.Runner` (`server/runner/s3presign/runner.go:17`), whose `CheckAndPresign` re-signs S3-backed attachment URLs in batches of 100, refreshing any presigned URL within 4 days of its 5-day expiry (`server/runner/s3presign/runner.go:46-133`).
- **Schedule:** once eagerly at startup, then every 12 hours (`runnerInterval = time.Hour * 12`, `server/runner/s3presign/runner.go:27`; ticker loop at `:29-41`).
- **Wiring:** `Server.startBackgroundRunners` — `server/server.go:153-176` (constructed `:162`, immediate `RunOnce` `:163`, goroutine `Run` `:169`), called from `Server.Start` at `server/server.go:129`.

**h02 — Outbound webhook delivery + SSRF protection**
- **Delivery function:** `webhook.Post` — `internal/webhook/webhook.go:120` (executes `safeClient.Do(req)` at `:152`). Async path: `webhook.PostAsync` (`:184`) enqueues onto `asyncPostQueue` (`:39`), drained by 4 goroutines started in `init()` (`:42-53`) that call `Post`.
- **Protection:** dial-time IP filtering — `safeClient`'s transport uses `safeDialContext` (`internal/webhook/webhook.go:32-37`, `:59-77`), which resolves the host and rejects reserved/private IPs via `isReservedIP` against `reservedCIDRs` (loopback, RFC-1918, link-local/169.254.169.254 IMDS, IPv6 equivalents) — `internal/webhook/validate.go:14-56`. Because the check happens at dial time after resolution, it also defeats DNS rebinding. A second, config-time check is `webhook.ValidateURL` (`internal/webhook/validate.go:62`), called when webhooks are created/updated (`server/router/api/v1/user_service_webhooks.go:74,161,182`). Escape hatch: `webhook.AllowPrivateIPs` (`internal/webhook/validate.go:41`).

**h03 — Identity providers**
- **Abstraction package:** `internal/idp` (`internal/idp/idp.go` — `IdentityProviderUserInfo`).
- **Implementation package:** `internal/idp/oauth2` (`internal/idp/oauth2/oauth2.go:19-41`, `NewIdentityProvider`, `ExchangeToken`, PKCE support). Only OAuth2/OIDC ships. Consumed at `server/router/api/v1/auth_service_sso.go:12-13`.

**h04 — Direct MySQL driver construction outside the factory**
- **No.** The only construction site is `mysql.NewDB(profile)` inside the factory `db.NewDBDriver` at `store/db/db.go:22`. Evidence: `grep -rn "mysql.NewDB\|db/mysql"` across all `.go` files returns exactly `store/db/db.go:8` (import) and `store/db/db.go:22` (call) — no test file constructs it either. (`store/test/containers.go:101` uses the unrelated `testcontainers-go/modules/mysql` container helper, not the store driver.)

**h05 — Emoji reactions on user delete**
- **Mechanism:** explicit Go code, per driver — no database-level cascade.
- **Evidence:** `store/db/sqlite/user_delete.go:96` (`deleteReactionsByContentIDsTx`, decl `:380`) and `:102` (`deleteReactionsByCreatorTx`, decl `:400`), inside the `DeleteUser` transaction (`:29`). Same at `store/db/postgres/user_delete.go:96,102,380,400` and `store/db/mysql/user_delete.go:96,102,417,437`. Schema check: `CREATE TABLE reaction` has no foreign key (`store/migration/sqlite/LATEST.sql:92-99`, `postgres/LATEST.sql:91-98`, `mysql/LATEST.sql`); the only `ON DELETE CASCADE` in the whole schema is on `memo_share.memo_id` (`store/migration/sqlite/LATEST.sql:109` and peers). Entry point: `Store.DeleteUser` → `driver.DeleteUser` (`store/user.go:171-181`).

**h06 — RPC handlers reaching an outbound user-configured URL**
Handlers (all in `server/router/api/v1/`):
- `CreateMemo` — `memo_service.go:70` → `DispatchMemoCreatedWebhook` (`memo_service.go:157`)
- `UpdateMemo` — `memo_service.go:401` → `dispatchMemoUpdatedSideEffects` (`memo_service.go:513`) → `DispatchMemoUpdatedWebhook` (`memo_update_helpers.go:67`)
- `DeleteMemo` — `memo_service.go:518` → `DispatchMemoDeletedWebhook` (`memo_service.go:562`)
- `CreateMemoComment` — `memo_service_comments.go:20` → `DispatchMemoCommentCreatedWebhook` (`memo_service_comments.go:119`)
- `SetMemoAttachments` (`memo_attachment_service.go:16` → `:48`) and `SetMemoRelations` (`memo_relation_service.go:16` → `:48`)

**Convergence function:** `webhook.PostAsync` — `internal/webhook/webhook.go:184` (all six paths call it at `memo_service_webhooks.go:43` and `:71`); actual HTTP send happens one hop later in `webhook.Post` — `internal/webhook/webhook.go:120`.

*(A separate, non-webhook outbound path exists: `GetLinkMetadata` fetches a user-supplied URL via `internal/httpgetter` — `server/router/api/v1/memo_service_link_metadata.go`.)*

**h07 — Profile-image request → stored data**
```
GET /file/users/:identifier/avatar   — server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:124 (route)
```

- **`(*filter.Engine).CompileToStatement` — `internal/filter/engine.go:74` — ~7 production call sites** (`internal/filter/helpers.go:11`, `server/router/api/v1/attachment_service.go:413`, `server/router/api/v1/shortcut_service.go:356`, `store/db/sqlite/memo_relation.go:85`, `store/db/postgres/memo_relation.go:87,98`, `store/db/mysql/memo_relation.go:78`), and ~38 more references once `internal/filter`'s tests are counted — by far the largest total.
